note: Day-1 reflective-loop baseline (Graph Engineering §VI.A; exit criterion = measured quality improvement). Ships UNMEASURED on purpose, under the same honesty invariant as trigger-evals.baseline.json: no quality number is written here until an authenticated `--measure` run produces one. The `coverage` block below is NOT a measurement — it is an inventory of which skills carry a rubric, refreshed by `node tools/skill-loop.mjs` with no model calls. The selftest scores in evals/runs/*.selftest.json are also NOT measurements: they are scores of hand-authored reference drafts and exist only to prove the rubrics discriminate.
method: tools/skill-loop.mjs --measure (reflective_task per Graph Engineering §VI.A): round 1 is the skill's first draft, each later round re-prompts with the criterion-level failures from the rubric's DETERMINISTIC head; stopping rule = score >= 1 or 5 rounds. Each round is one headless session at --max-turns 50, granted Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash — the shell is part of the measured configuration because task-executor uses one to run its own T0 probes in production, and a session denied it aborts rather than producing a number. n is per-row and printed in the results table — 10 for four skills, 3 for solution-architect, which already met condition 4 and was therefore out of scope for the n=10 pass. The graded artifact is the DELIVERABLE FILE, not the transcript, and each revision round starts from the previous round's deliverable in a fresh directory — so a round edits one artifact rather than re-drawing it. Runs before 2026-08-04 did NOT carry it forward and are re-sampling, not revision; they are not comparable on delta. Oracle criteria are scored per ROW (fraction of contract rows passing), not all-or-nothing; `satisfied` still requires every row, so approve_at is unchanged in meaning. Runs before 2026-08-04 scored these criteria binary and recorded 0.0 for any artifact short of perfect. Quality rates are MODEL-DEPENDENT — this baseline describes the model named below and no other. Scored by regex detectors, NOT by a model judge, and the two shapes do not generalize equally: an ANCHOR-shaped criterion (a file:line, an un-ticked AC box, a verdict token the skill's own output contract defines) is hit by a real transcript for the same reason the fixture hits it, while a PHRASE-shaped one matches a particular way of writing an inference and scores a paraphrase of the same bad conclusion as clean - those are the weakest criteria in any rubric here. Every criterion also carries an assertion field, the question a model judge would be asked, so a second and general head can be built over the same rubric without restating the criteria.

withdrawn.reason: PROXY ARTIFACT — not a measurement of skill quality. The headless adapter ran at --max-turns 12; the CLI exhausted the budget and printed `Error: Reached max turns (12)` (29 bytes) on stdout with exit 0. The adapter's broken-harness guard only rejected EMPTY output, so that error string was scored against the rubric as if it were the model's draft. An independent run on claude-sonnet-5 produced a byte-identical 29-byte draft, confirming the cause is the harness and not the model. Withdrawn, not carried forward — the same disposition the prior trigger-eval TPR was given (audit F1).
withdrawn.fixed_by: generateWithClaude() now rejects CLI error sentinels and sub-120-byte output; default --max-turns raised 12 -> 50.

withdrawn.reason: PERMISSION-BLOCKED — the delta is an artifact, not skill quality. The headless probe ran with no permission grant, so the skill could not execute `node` to probe the running build. Its round-3 reply was verbatim: 'I need permission to run the Node.js process to probe the build.' That is CORRECT behaviour — it refused to fabricate an observation it could not make — and it scores 0, so a 0.571 first draft 'regressed' to 0. Compounded by the revision prompt not demanding a complete artifact, so the model answered with a plan instead of a report. NOTE: v1=0.571 is itself a valid first-draft score; only the DELTA is invalid.
withdrawn.fixed_by: adapter now passes --allowedTools Read Glob Grep 'Bash(node:*)'; revision prompt now demands the COMPLETE report and forbids reporting unobserved results.

withdrawn.reason: HD-004 — NOT a measurement of skill quality. All three runs wrote task frontmatter as YAML BLOCK SEQUENCES, and board-derive.mjs's private `listField` read only the inline `[a, b]` form. Every list field on every task therefore came back EMPTY: `use_case_refs` (so UC-ANCHOR went red for all of them), `touched_files` (so the external-fact row reported 'none did'), and `depends_on`/`unlocks` — the last pair empty in BOTH directions, so edge-symmetry passed VACUOUSLY. This is the second instance of HD-003: the same defect had just been fixed in contract-md.mjs, and the repo turned out to have a SECOND hand-rolled frontmatter parser for the same documented format. Re-scored under the fix, the identical stored drafts read 9/10, 9/10 and 10/10 rather than 8/10 across the board. A second, smaller apparatus fault rode along: the fixture prompt said use_case_refs must 'match a use-case FILENAME' while its own example showed the bare id, and all three runs wrote `UC-01.md`, which is the filename and which the lint does not resolve. Withdrawn rather than superseded because the number describes the harness, not the skill — the same disposition the max-turns and permission-denial artifacts were given. Successor: fixture e275807eff45902b.

limitations: CONDITION 4 WAS AMENDED BY THE OPERATOR ON 2026-08-04, AFTER THESE RESULTS WERE KNOWN, AND THE AMENDMENT MAKES ALL FIVE SKILLS PASS. That is the exact shape of a bar moved to fit its data, so it is disclosed at the top of this list rather than left for a reader to notice. THE ORIGINAL TEXT — 'at least one run needed more than one round' — READ 3 OF 5, and it is preserved verbatim in docs/internal/plan/ratchet-and-receipt-plan.md §1 beside the amendment. The amended text reads DEMONSTRATED OR RESOLVED: a skill satisfies condition 4 by showing a revision, or by drawing enough runs to BOUND its rate — zero revisions across n >= 10 runs of one unchanged instrument, with the bound published. THREE THINGS ARGUE AGAINST READING IT AS RETUNING, AND NONE IS CONCLUSIVE. (1) The threshold references a power requirement and no measured value: a true revision rate of 1/3 is detected with at least 95% probability once n >= 8, so ten draws clear it with margin. RESOLVED_N is exported and structural §48 fails if it drops below what that calculation supports. (2) The mechanism half of the old condition is UNCHANGED and enforced mechanically for every skill — §48 requires each SELFTEST to drive its committed partial reference to strong through a revision round with a positive delta — so a rubric that cannot revise at all still fails by construction, independently of anything a model does. (3) The decision was the OPERATOR'S, taken at a gate. Under this repo's own separation of duties that is where a bar decision belongs; the author declined to move it, because §7.1 forbids changing a bar after seeing which subjects fail it. THE CASE ON THE MERITS IS THAT THE OLD CRITERION WAS NOT REPRODUCIBLE. As an existence claim over a sample its answer moved with n and with luck while the skill held still, and ba-pitch-analyzer's verdict flipped THREE TIMES on a fixture that never changed a byte. WHAT A READER SHOULD CARRY IS THE RATE, NOT THE VERDICT: 10% and 33% and 6.3% for the three that demonstrate a revision, and <= 21% for the two that bound one.

THE HEADLINE IS THAT CONDITION 4 WAS NEVER A PROPERTY OF THE SKILLS ALONE — IT WAS A PROPERTY OF n. Measured at n=3 it read three skills, then one, then two, and then three again once the pooled reading was applied. Nothing about any skill changed across those readings. Condition 4 AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN is a threshold on a COUNT OF RUNS ('at least one run needed more than one round'), so at n=3 a skill whose true revision rate is 1/3 shows nothing 30% of the time and one whose rate is 6% shows something 18% of the time. Both errors happened here, in both directions, and were published as findings before being caught: ba-pitch-analyzer's MET was a one-in-five event on a rate now measured at 6.3%, and scope-architect's retraction was a miss on a skill that does revise. AT n=10 THE PICTURE IS STABLE: scope-architect 1/10 (four rounds in that run), ba-pitch-analyzer 0/10 in the draw and 1/16 pooled, spec-evaluator 0/10, task-executor 0/10.

WHAT CONDITION 4 NOW SAYS, SKILL BY SKILL, WITH THE ARITHMETIC ITS SAMPLE EARNS — and the verdicts matter less than the rates beside them. scope-architect: 1 revision in 10 on the current fixture, MET, and that revision is a FOUR-ROUND chain, the longest ever recorded here. solution-architect: 1 in 3, MET, and uniquely it has revised in five independent measurements across five instrument versions, so its verdict rests on reproduction rather than one draw — but it is the ONLY skill still measured at n=3 and its bound is correspondingly wide (86.5%). ba-pitch-analyzer: 1 in 16 pooled on a byte-identical fixture, MET on the pooled reading and 0/10 on the current draw, rate 6.3%, bound 26.4%. task-executor and spec-evaluator: 0 in 13 pooled each, bound 20.6% — they satisfy the amended condition on its RESOLVED branch, which is a weaker claim than the other three and is labelled as such in the results table. A BOUND, NOT A PROOF; the honest claim is 'below roughly 21%', never 'never'.

THE DIAL-THREE HYPOTHESIS NOW HAS A HELD-OUT TEST, AND IT PASSED — the one thing the previous revision of this file said was missing. That version recorded, as its own harshest caveat, that the hypothesis was 'formed after dials one and two failed, tested on skills whose fixtures were being rewritten at the same time, and has no held-out case', and it named the fix: fix the recipe, apply it to a case that played no part in forming it, predict in writing beforehand. Done, and committed to git before a dollar was spent (docs/internal/plan/ratchet-and-receipt-plan.md §P7, commit e780d94). THE PREDICTION WAS THAT BOTH CEILINGED SKILLS WOULD REVISE, on the diagnosis that their earlier fixtures had INSTRUCTED the check the external-fact row was supposed to measure ('READ IT before you write anything that touches the store'; 'probe each Test-Surface row the way the row is written'). Each fixture gained one row whose fact is pointed at nowhere. BOTH PREDICTIONS FAILED: 3/3 first drafts, both skills. task-executor's drafts edited a store writer nothing they touched imports and named the trap in prose; spec-evaluator's cited an amendment file by path and line. So the hypothesis this baseline already held — that dial three produces headroom only where the check is optional AND THE MODEL ACTUALLY SKIPS IT — predicted the outcome, and my competing diagnosis did not. A confirmation is worth something only when the test could have gone the other way, and this one did go the other way for the person who designed it.

SCORING IS DETERMINISTIC, NOT A MODEL JUDGE. Every row of all five rubrics delegates to a script that already grades the artifact (spec-lint, trace-lint, board-derive, the process oracle). No model judge is involved anywhere in Tier 1, deliberately — a judge head would re-introduce the authorship this tier exists to remove.

THREE ESCALATION DIALS ACROSS SEVENTEEN PAID MEASUREMENTS. Dial one, COMPLEXITY of a single artifact (task-executor 6 contract rows -> 12 with batch selectors; spec-evaluator a second planted bug reachable only by a seeded probe): no movement. Dial two, VOLUME of mutually-consistent constraints (ba-pitch-analyzer 9 tasks/8 edges -> 20 tasks/36 edges; scope-architect 17 files/8 tasks -> 36 files/20 tasks against a cap forcing a five-way split): no movement, and the escalations demonstrably landed — one first draft computed a 27-edge inverse map correctly, another produced seven cap-compliant disjoint scopes covering twenty tasks. Dial three, AGREEMENT WITH A FACT OUTSIDE THE ARTIFACT: it is the only dial that has ever produced a revision. At n=10 it sustains a DEMONSTRATED revision in three of five skills (scope-architect 1/10, solution-architect 1/3, ba-pitch-analyzer 1/16 pooled) and a bounded rate of <= 21% in the other two. Every fixture named here ships a committed PARTIAL reference scoring strictly between its weak and strong ones, so none of these ranges are notional.

SEVENTEEN SUPERSEDED FIXTURES FOR FIVE SKILLS IN TWO DAYS. Every change is declared and both numbers are published, which is what the no-retuning rule requires — but the RATE is its own caveat, and the honest summary is that these numbers describe fixtures designed over two days by one author. Two things argue against reading that as tuning toward the answer, and neither is conclusive: each change had a stated hypothesis written before the run, and the last two changes were pre-registered in git and PREDICTED THE WRONG OUTCOME, which is the opposite of an instrument tuned until it produces the movement its author wanted.

WHAT THE REVISIONS ACTUALLY FIXED WAS CONFORMANCE AND DILIGENCE, NOT REASONING — and the n=10 run makes this sharper rather than softer. scope-architect's four-round run failed the SAME ROW every time, SA-FIXTURES, on a different scope's e2e command each round: `archive`, then `capture`, then `capture` again in another form. Each defect was only reachable once the previous was cleared, so the loop did four passes of incremental work rather than one correction re-scored three times — which is the most loop-like behaviour anything here has produced. It is still a declared command that does not run, not a reasoning failure. solution-architect's rounds are the same family: a table under the wrong heading, engines named without being traced. The loop demonstrably moves real scores by acting on criterion-level defects, which is what Table II asks for. It has never shown a skill REASONING better on a second pass, and no number here supports that claim.

EXIT CRITERION IS `final_score >= approve_at`, not `delta > 0`. Under the old delta rule a perfect 3/3 run reads 'NOT met' — the criterion penalised a skill that was already right. Changed with explicit operator authorisation after the flaw was measured, not quietly. The `revised?` column carries what the delta rule used to. Since the 2026-08-04 amendment it has three states rather than two: a DEMONSTRATED revision, a RESOLVED rate (zero revisions over n >= 10 pooled runs, which reads 'MET — rate bounded'), and UNRESOLVED (zero revisions and too few runs to bound them), which is the only one that still reads 'exit criterion only'.

VACUOUS TRUTH IS THE HAZARD SPECIFIC TO A LINT-DELEGATED RUBRIC, and one instance shipped before being caught. A lint reports no finding for an artifact that does not exist, so 'no PA1 violation' is trivially true of an empty scopes/ directory. Every row renderer now fails ALL of its rows when the artifact it grades is absent, and structural §48(d1b) asserts a seed-only workspace scores exactly 0 (or, for a brownfield fixture, below the strong bar). The instance that got through: WM-REACH excluded unresolvable engines and reported 'all 6 engines reach the entry point' for a map where six of six had never resolved.

SCOPE OF EVERY NUMBER HERE: ONE fixture per skill, 5 of 13 skills instrumented (the honest ceiling is 6 of 13 — five Tier-1 plus translator), and every live number is claude-sonnet-5. n IS NOW 10 FOR FOUR SKILLS AND STILL 3 FOR solution-architect, which is an asymmetry a reader must not smooth over: the one skill whose MET rests on the smallest sample is the one that was never re-drawn, because it already met the condition and was therefore out of scope for the n=10 pass. Its case is carried by reproduction across five instruments instead. A quality rate is MODEL-dependent AND FIXTURE-dependent AND SAMPLE-dependent, and this file now demonstrates the third of those rather than merely asserting it.

THE MEASUREMENT HAS NOW FOUND FIVE PRODUCTION DEFECTS AND THAT IS STILL WORTH MORE THAN THE SCORES. All five are one family — the committed contract format FAILS SILENT — and all five surfaced because a real worker wrote a real committed artifact and a real gate read it. HD-001: a table under an unrecognised heading parses empty, and trace-lint reports green '0/0 engines reach' for a wiring map holding six correct rows. HD-002: a quoted list member split on its own commas, turning a worker's honest TBD note into four bogus entries on a field t0-verify EXECUTES. HD-003/HD-004: a YAML block sequence discarded whole — and the repo turned out to have TWO hand-rolled parsers for one documented format, so fixing the first left the second silently returning empty and cost a full paid measurement. HD-005, new in this revision (2026-08-04): a path written as a markdown CODE SPAN parses as a filename containing backticks, so the same gate HD-001 made fail OPEN was also made to fail CLOSED — six unresolvable engines reported for a map in which all six resolve and reach. All five are fixed, pinned by structural §46(f)(g)(h)(i), and mutation-verified in both directions. THE PATTERN MATTERS MORE THAN THE BUGS: every one of them first appeared as a SKILL scoring badly. An eval not instrumented to tell harness failure from skill failure will under-report skill quality and read as a confident measurement while doing it.

THE `approve_at` OF ba-pitch-analyzer WAS RAISED 0.85 -> 1.0 BY THIS AUTHOR when its external-fact row was added, with a justification written before that run (GATE L1b's own condition is spec-lint red == 0, so every structural row passing IS the gate's bar). THAT CHANGE SUPPORTS A LIVE VERDICT AGAIN AND THE READER MUST BE TOLD SO. An earlier revision of this file said the change 'no longer supports any live verdict', which was true for exactly as long as ba-pitch-analyzer's MET was withdrawn; the pooled reading restored it, and the caveat had quietly decayed into a false reassurance. Under the original approve_at of 0.85 the run that produced this skill's only observed revision would have approved on its first draft and no revision would have been recorded. scope-architect's approve_at was 1.0 from its fixture's creation, before any measurement, and solution-architect's has been 0.9 throughout — neither of those verdicts depends on a bar that moved.

RAISING n FROM 3 TO 10 COST $47.92 AGAINST A ~$33 ESTIMATE, AND THE ERROR IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN RANDOM. Every skill overran: task-executor $6.70 (est. $6.30), ba-pitch-analyzer $7.98 ($5.30), spec-evaluator $12.56 ($8.60), scope-architect $20.70 ($12.90). The estimate multiplied each skill's measured per-run cost at n=3 by 10, which assumes runs are independent draws of equal cost. They are not: scope-architect moved 444,721 output tokens at n=10 against roughly 78,512 at n=3, more than five times the tokens for 3.3 times the runs, because one run needed FOUR rounds and a round's cost is dominated by re-reading the session preamble. THE CORRECT UNIT FOR A BUDGET IS ROUNDS x RUNS, NOT RUNS — and the runs that make a measurement worth taking are exactly the multi-round ones that blow the estimate.

WHAT THE §1 BAR SAID BEFORE IT WAS AMENDED, KEPT BECAUSE THE AMENDMENT IS RECENT AND THE READER SHOULD SEE BOTH. Under the ORIGINAL condition-4 text — 'at least one run needed more than one round' — this file read THREE OF FIVE: scope-architect, solution-architect and ba-pitch-analyzer met it; task-executor and spec-evaluator did not, having never needed a second round in any measurement on any fixture. The programme was stopped there rather than buying more, and those reasons still stand on their own terms: a third fixture escalation for the two was ruled out IN ADVANCE by a pre-registration committed before any spend (docs/internal/plan/ratchet-and-receipt-plan.md §P7, commit e780d94), because two pre-registered predictions had already failed and a third attempt is indistinguishable from tuning an instrument until it yields the answer its author wanted; and raising n further would have cost roughly $52-70 for a 55-87% chance of one observation, leaving the same bound if it observed none. THE AMENDMENT DID NOT BUY THOSE RUNS, IT CHANGED WHAT COUNTS — see the first entry in this list, which is where that decision is disclosed.

CONDITION 4 AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN WAS A BADLY-FORMED CRITERION AND THIS FILE IS THE EVIDENCE — a finding about the PLAN rather than about any skill, and it is what the amendment was made to fix. 'At least one run needed more than one round' is an existence claim over a sample, so its answer moves with n and with luck while the skill stays put: ba-pitch-analyzer's verdict flipped THREE TIMES on a fixture that never changed a byte. A criterion a reader cannot reproduce from the same instrument is measuring the draw, not the loop. The operator amended it on 2026-08-04 to DEMONSTRATED OR RESOLVED and the disclosure sits at the top of this list. WHAT SURVIVES EITHER READING IS THE RATE AND ITS BOUND, which is why every row carries them and why they should be read in preference to the yes/no.

scope-architect: RE-MEASURED AT n=10 on claude-sonnet-5, fixture c613665dbb8e9202: v1 0.983 [0.833, 1] -> final 1.0, ONE OF TEN RUNS NEEDED FOUR ROUNDS, approve 10/10. $20.6953 — by far the most expensive row in this file.

CONDITION 4 HOLDS, AND ONLY n=10 COULD SHOW IT. Runs 1-4 approved on the first draft; run 5 needed FOUR rounds; runs 6-10 approved on the first draft. A three-run sample drawn from the front of this sequence sees nothing, which is exactly what the n=3 measurement reported. THE LONGEST REVISION CHAIN EVER RECORDED HERE — every previous one was two rounds.

WHAT THE FOUR ROUNDS ACTUALLY DID, from the stored records, and it is a sequence rather than one fix: round 1 failed SA-FIXTURES on the `archive` scope's e2e command; round 2 failed the SAME ROW on the `capture` scope's command; round 3 failed it again on `capture`, now written as `! node src/cli/main.js ...`; round 4 approved. Each defect was only reachable once the previous one was cleared, so the loop did four passes of genuinely incremental work rather than one correction re-scored three times.

EVERY ONE OF THOSE FAILURES IS THE EXTERNAL-FACT ROW. SA-FIXTURES asks whether a declared `e2e_verification_fixture` RUNS GREEN against the codebase as it stands — a property of the build, not of the artifact, and one the model must go and execute rather than reason about. Dial three is the only dial that has ever produced a revision in this repo, and this is its clearest instance.

THE n=3 AND n=10 NUMBERS ARE NOT A CLEAN BEFORE/AFTER, and the fingerprint says so: d5725a654df6f936 -> c613665dbb8e9202. The HD-005 fix changed contract-md.mjs, which is in this fixture's contract_files, so the instrument moved between the two. What n=10 establishes is a fresh measurement on the CURRENT instrument; what it cannot establish is that the same skill on the same instrument would have shown 0/3 and then 1/10.

SO THE EARLIER RETRACTION OF THIS SKILL'S MET WAS WRONG IN ITS CONCLUSION AND RIGHT IN ITS CAUTION. It was reported as having lost condition 4; it has not lost it, it was measured with too few draws to see it. That is published here rather than quietly corrected, because a retraction that itself needed retracting is evidence about this instrument's resolution and nothing else in this file records it.

THE ROW DELEGATES TO t0-verify's OWN RUNNER (`runFixtures`), so a fixture is graded exactly as GATE L2 will grade it — `shell: true`, pass iff exit 0 — rather than by a second runner that would drift from it.

THREE OF SIX ROWS ARE AUTHORED (SA-PRESENT, SA-COVERAGE, SA-FIXTURES) and each is named as such here. SA-FIXTURES' criterion is SKILL.md's own sentence — 'too speculative to fixture -> mark TBD and flag it, never invent a fixture for unbuilt behavior'.
solution-architect: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-04 on claude-sonnet-5, n=3, fixture 6fada177c6343ebc: v1 0.889 [0.667, 1] -> final 1.0, delta +0.111, improved 1/3, approve 3/3, ONE OF THREE RUNS NEEDED A SECOND ROUND. $1.7336.

THE MOST REPRODUCIBLE OF THE THREE THAT DEMONSTRATE A REVISION. Across five independent measurements on five instrument versions its revision step has executed every time (48943f1ee789b6e9, 8bfbe80b203aeecd, 552554ed2fc9d53e, b5cd095f515c9531, 6fada177c6343ebc). scope-architect's is now also demonstrated, at n=10, and ba-pitch-analyzer's on the pooled reading of sixteen runs — but each of those rests on a single observation in its sample, where this one has reproduced across every instrument it has been measured on. A property that reproduces across five instruments is a property of the task; one that appears once is a sample. THE CAVEAT THAT RIDES WITH IT: this is the only skill still measured at n=3, so its own bound is the widest in the file (86.5%) and its rate estimate the least precise. It was out of scope for the n=10 pass precisely because it already met the condition, which is how the smallest sample ended up under the strongest-looking verdict.

THIS RUN EXISTS BECAUSE THE PREVIOUS ONE FOUND HD-005, and all three readings are published because two of them are of a broken instrument. AS MEASURED under the defective parser (fixture b5cd095f515c9531, retained under superseded): v1 0.333, final 0.889 [0.667, 1], approve 2/3 — run 3 stopped on no_improvement at 0.667. RE-SCORED, same stored drafts, backticks stripped and nothing else changed: that round is 1.0, so the loop would have stopped at round 2 with approve 3/3. RE-MEASURED under the shipped fix: the row above. The re-score is the evidence about the INSTRUMENT because it holds the drafts fixed; the re-measure is the number, because it is the only one taken through the code that now ships. The three must not be subtracted from one another.

WHAT THE REVISION ROUND ACTUALLY FIXED, from the stored artifacts: run 3's first draft named engines it had not traced to the entry point, scoring 0.667 on WM-ENGINE-RESOLVES and WM-REACH; the second round corrected them. In earlier measurements the round-1 defect was the `## Wiring` heading (HD-001's shape) rather than reachability. These are CONFORMANCE and DILIGENCE defects, not reasoning defects. The loop demonstrably moved a real score by acting on a criterion-level defect, which is what Table II asks for; it did NOT demonstrate that the skill reasoned better on the second pass. Only the first is being claimed.

THE FIXTURE HAS NEVER BEEN CHANGED AFTER SEEING WHICH ROWS FAILED, across all five measurements. Three failure modes looked like apparatus artifacts and the plan's §0 derivability audit ruled against a fixture change on two of them: the `## Wiring` heading is stated in the fixture prompt, and a bare engine path is stated in the skill's own SKILL.md.
